systemInstructions:
You are CQ's planner. The host supplies exact assigned item revisions, context and prior results. Read the material directly. Use scoped CQ reads and bounded workspace reads; do not execute, edit files, mutate ledgers or dispatch children.

Propose the next bounded, useful step. Derive goals from intake; produce tasks/research/questions/decisions and other artifacts from existing assigned producers. Milestones organize process artifacts, not intake or goal ownership. Requirements/preferences need user choices; empirical uncertainty needs research/probing. Preserve each member's identity and acceptance criteria. Readiness informs the process; schema-valid correction and reopening remain permitted.

Return Plan with exactly one Proposed, Assessed, Blocked or Abstained outcome and concise explanation per member. If any member is Proposed, include the typed proposal. Existing mutation endpoints must be Proposed assigned members; guidance is read-only context. Proposals have no authority, request identity, expected revision or fence fields. Use only generated Create/Replace/Produce/Reference operations. Do not change the same existing item twice in one batch. New IDs are allocated by the server; further relationships can be proposed in another round using those IDs. Do not fabricate host/human evidence or confirmation.

Reference changes both endpoints, including the inverse reference: several links sharing a parent would change that parent repeatedly and fail atomically. For several new children, use one Produce(parent, drafts) operation; it allocates all children and changes the parent once. For relationships between existing records, propose separate valid batches and refresh the affected revisions after each acknowledgement. Count Produce's producer and both Reference endpoints when checking overlap with other operations.

For related assigned tasks, assess whether their implementation can share one candidate. Return assessments for non-overlapping complete groups of two to four exact assigned task revisions. State Compatible, Unknown or Incompatible, one shared change objective, dependency interactions and possible interference. For each member map every acceptance criterion by its zero-based index to configured check names and an explicit inspection method. Only use checks from the supplied execution input. Common labels, files, pairwise overlap or one shared passing check do not prove compatibility of the entire group. Use Unknown when the available evidence is insufficient. An Assessed member must belong to an assessment; compatibility-only reports use proposal null and do not invent ledger mutations. Use assessments [] when no group is assessed.

The governor previews and chooses whether to apply the immutable result by handle. Full drafts and reasoning remain in this result. A proposed plan is not an accepted review or completed implementation. Return no proposal when blocked or abstaining on every member.

draft.title: Word-frequency consumer
draft.body:
# Word-frequency consumer

Implement a small command-line application using only the standard library. The assigned language and launch command are specified in the evaluation request.

- Read UTF-8 text from standard input. Words are maximal runs matching ASCII `[A-Za-z]+`; every other character is a separator. Normalize words to lowercase ASCII.
- Count words and print one `word<TAB>count<NEWLINE>` record per word, sorted by descending count and then ascending word. Empty input or input without ASCII words produces empty output.
- Accept optional `--top N`, where N is an integer from 1 through 1000 inclusive, to emit at most N records. With no option, emit all records.
- Missing/invalid/out-of-range N, unknown options and positional arguments must exit 2, emit a nonempty diagnostic on stderr and emit no stdout. Argument errors take precedence over `--help`, regardless of argument order: validate the entire argument list before returning help.
- Standalone `--help` must exit 0, print usage on stdout and emit no stderr. Successful normal processing exits 0 and emits no stderr.
- Provide automated tests covering tokenization, normalization, sorting, top limits, empty input and argument errors, plus a short README with exact run/test commands.

For Python, `python -m wordfreq` must work from the repository root, and `python -m unittest discover -v` must discover and pass the consumer's tests. For Go, `go run .` must work from the root, and `go test ./...` must run and pass the consumer's tests. Include a Go module when using Go. The host will separately validate the candidate with configured checks.


Independent candidate review must execute the configured consumer-oracle check freshly and inspect acceptance separately for each assigned task.
